plan: - MCU: Arduino Uno or ESP32 with GRBL firmware- Actuators: NEMA 17 stepper motors (3x), corresponding stepper drivers (e.g., A4988 or DRV8825)- Power: 12-24V power supply, wiring, end-stop switches- Mechanical: Aluminum extrusion frame (2020 or 2040), lead screws or ball screws, linear rails/bearings, spindle motor with ER11 collet- Custom 3D prints: Motor mounts, lead screw nuts, spindle mount, tool holder- Enclosure: Optional acrylic or wood dust enclosure

nodes.name: Main Controller

research.summary: The ESP32 Dev Kit C V4 is a powerful development board built around the ESP32-WROOM-32 module, offering integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth for versatile connectivity. It features a dual-core processor, substantial flash and SRAM, and numerous GPIOs, making it excellent for IoT applications and demanding embedded tasks. Its robust capabilities are particularly well-suited for running GRBL firmware to control CNC axes and spindles, providing a cost-effective and high-performance solution for the Desktop CNC Mill project.

subSteps.title: 3D print all custom parts (motor mounts, lead screw nut blocks, spindle mount, carriage plates, end-stop mounts, controller enclosure, tool holder)
Cut or prepare MDF spoilboard to size
Deburr and clean all 3D printed parts for smooth operation and fit
Test fit linear bearings (LM8UU) onto linear rods (8mm)
Wire the main 24V power supply to the buck converter, all stepper drivers, and the spindle motor driver

detail.tip: Ensure correct polarity for all 24V connections. Use appropriate wire gauge (e.g., 18-22 AWG) for power distribution to prevent voltage drop and overheating.
steps: Connect the V+ output of the Main 24V Power Supply to the VIN+ input of the 24V to 5V Converter.
Connect the V- (GND) output of the Main 24V Power Supply to the VIN- input of the 24V to 5V Converter.
Wire the V+ output of the Main 24V Power Supply to the VMOT pins of the X-Axis Stepper Driver, Y-Axis Stepper Driver, and Z-Axis Stepper Driver.
Wire the V- (GND) output of the Main 24V Power Supply to the GND pins of the X-Axis Stepper Driver, Y-Axis Stepper Driver, and Z-Axis Stepper Driver.
Connect the V+ output of the Main 24V Power Supply to the Vin+ input of the Spindle Motor Driver.
Connect the V- (GND) output of the Main 24V Power Supply to the Vin- input of the Spindle Motor Driver.
detail.summary: Wire 24V power from the main supply to the buck converter, stepper drivers, and spindle driver.

subSteps.title: Connect the 5V output from the buck converter to the ESP32, logic VCC for all stepper drivers, and all end-stop switches
Connect stepper motors to their respective stepper drivers
Connect the spindle motor to the spindle motor driver
Wire ESP32 GPIO pins to stepper driver STEP, DIR, EN pins (D14/D12/D13 for X, D27/D26/D25 for Y, D33/D32/D16 for Z)
Connect ESP32 PWM pin (D4) to the spindle motor driver PWM input
Connect end-stop switch signal pins to ESP32 GPIO pins (D19 for X, D18 for Y, D5 for Z)
Perform continuity checks on all power and signal lines to verify correct wiring
Flash GRBL firmware onto the ESP32 microcontroller
Configure GRBL settings for stepper motor steps/mm, max feedrates, and acceleration
Test individual stepper motor movement and verify correct direction for X, Y, and Z axes
Verify end-stop switch functionality and homing sequence in GRBL
Test spindle motor ON/OFF and speed control via GRBL commands
Assemble the base frame using aluminum extrusions (base_frame_x_front_back, base_frame_y_side) and corner brackets with M5 hardware
Mount Y-axis linear rods (y_linear_rods) to the base frame and install Y-axis lead screw (y_axis_lead_screw) with KP08 pillow block bearings
Assemble the Y-axis gantry (y_gantry_beam, y_gantry_plates) with LM8UU bearings and attach to the Y-axis lead screw via the printed nut block (y_lead_screw_nut_block)
Mount the Y-axis stepper motor (y_stepper_motor) to its mount (y_motor_mount) and connect to the lead screw with a shaft coupler
Assemble the X-axis carriage (x_carriage_plate), linear rods, lead screw, and bearings, then mount it to the Y-axis gantry beam
Mount the X-axis stepper motor (x_stepper_motor) and connect to its lead screw

Assemble the Z-axis (z_axis_vertical_extrusions, z_carriage_plate, z_linear_rods, z_axis_lead_screw, z_stepper_motor) and mount to the X-axis carriage plate; attach the spindle motor (spindle_motor) to the printed spindle mount (spindle_mount)
Install all end-stop switches onto their 3D printed mounts and attach mounts to the frame/axes at travel limits
Mount the spoilboard to the base frame and perform final cable management and routing

projectDescription: A desktop CNC mill utilizing an ESP32 with GRBL firmware controls NEMA 17 stepper motors for precise XYZ motion. Linear rods and lead screws guide the ER11 spindle motor, all powered by a 24V supply and housed within an aluminum extrusion frame. End-stops ensure accurate homing and limit detection.

assumptions: Computer with USB port and Arduino IDE/PlatformIO installed
Basic knowledge of GRBL firmware flashing and configuration
Access to appropriate CAD software for 3D print file preparation if modifications are needed
